title: Linear Generator Networks for Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations
claim: A structured per-mode linear generator, split into conservative and dissipative parts, yields stability and spectral analysis within a nonlinear-lift pipeline.
layout: Top left-to-right pipeline row, with tree branching downward into generator and eigenvalue properties
description: A rounded-box diagram with three tiers. The top row is a left-to-right pipeline: input ω(x,y,T) in beige, a green Encoder (Koopman lift to r channels), a blue FFT, a highlighted purple box exp(L_k·t) per mode k, a blue IFFT, a green Decoder (r→1), and output ω̂(x,y,t) in beige. A line drops from the exp box to a purple box L_k = S − D_k. That box splits into a red box and a blue box. The red box gives S = (P − Pᵀ)/2, skew-symmetric and shared across k, and sits next to a red-green heatmap of an antisymmetric coupling matrix. The blue box gives D_k = diag(d + α|k|²/k²_max), and sits next to a blue diagonal-matrix heatmap. At the bottom, an 'Eigenvalues of L_k' box branches into three purple boxes: Spectral relations, Stability (Re λ ≤ 0) and Continuous time. The eye goes first to the top pipeline row.
caption: LGN-KM architecture. Input nonlinear data is lifted to $r$ channels via a spectral encoder, transformed to Fourier space, and propagated by the matrix exponential $\exp(L_k\,t)$ of a per-mode generator $L_k = S - D_k$. The skew-symmetric component $S = (P - P^{\top})/2$ is shared across all wavevectors. The positive-definite diagonal $D_k = \mathrm{diag}\!\left(d + \alpha |k|^{2}/k_{\max}^{2}\right)$ varies per wavevector and encodes mode-selective dissipation with learned base damping $d$ and Laplacian coefficient $\alpha$. The eigenvalues of $L_k$ are guaranteed to have non-positive real parts, enabling a complete spectral characterization of the dynamics across $r \times M^{2}$ eigenvalues, long-horizon stability, and continuous-time evaluation at arbitrary $t$ via a single matrix exponentiation.
abstract: Most physical systems are governed by nonlinear partial differential equations, yet the analytical tools that make linear systems transparent, such as eigenspectra, dispersion relations and modal decomposition, remain unavailable in nonlinear settings. We introduce Linear Generator Network-Koopman (LGN-KM), a neural operator that learns a nonlinear lift and a continuous-time linear generator for the lifted dynamics through the decomposition $L_k = S - D_k$, where $S$ is skew-symmetric (conservative coupling) and $D_k$ is positive-definite diagonal (mode-selective dissipation). The decomposition guarantees stability by construction and exposes the eigenstructure directly, making linear-systems analysis available on a nonlinear PDE. On 2D Navier-Stokes turbulence, the generator yields a complete multi-branch dispersion relation and models trained independently at viscosities $100\times$ apart learn the same coupling spectrum ($R^2 = 0.87$). The same architecture shows the corresponding diffusive damping on FitzHugh-Nagumo reaction-diffusion, and for pulse propagation in optical fibers, the oscillation frequencies of the learned generator match the fiber's dispersion relation, giving the group-velocity dispersion to within $3.1\%$ with no fitted constant. The architecture additionally enables long-horizon stability, $O(1)$ continuous-time evaluation, and physics-informed cross-regime model transfer.
